mstts:express-as.prosody: As we wrap up, let's remember—this story of American segregation isn't just about the past. It's really a call to notice, to take responsibility, and to step up. The world we live in was shaped by choices, and the world we leave behind? That’s up to the choices we make right now. Those lines that divide us— they're not set in stone. People made them, and people can change them. So, what should you take from all this? First, segregation didn’t just happen by accident—government policies drew those lines, not just individual choices. Second, the legacy of redlining and exclusion still affects who gets access to good schools, wealth, and opportunities today. Third, even though legal victories matter, real progress takes ongoing effort and constant watchfulness. And maybe most important—communities have always found ways to push back, to build strength and hope, even when it seemed impossible. The work of repair and justice? It’s possible. But only if we face the truth—and act together. If you’ve ever wondered why some neighborhoods seem to flourish while others are left struggling, or why opportunity feels out of reach for so many, the answer isn’t just in what’s happening today—it’s right there in our history. But here’s the thing: the past doesn’t have to keep us trapped. By learning about this history, by sharing it, and by refusing to settle for the world as it is, you’re helping write the story of change. Sure, it’s tough. The path forward isn’t always clear. But every honest conversation, every act of standing together, every small effort to redraw those lines—that’s another step toward a future where everyone truly belongs. The story of segregation isn’t over. And neither is the story of justice. The next chapter? That’s ours to write—together.
